20 What are the units of stress, strain and the Young modulus?
stress
strain
Young
modulus
A
newton
metre

B
newton

hints: Recall that stress is defined as force divided by cross-sectional area, $\text{stress} = F/A$, so check what unit $\text{N m}^{-2}$ corresponds to.
Recall that strain is defined as extension divided by original length, $\text{strain} = x/L$, so compare the units on top and bottom.
Recall that Young modulus is $\text{stress}/\text{strain}$, so dividing by a quantity with no unit must leave the unit of stress.
walkthrough: Start from the definitions: stress $= F/A$ where $F$ is in $\text{N}$ and $A$ is in $\text{m}^2$, and strain $= x/L$ where both $x$ and $L$ are in $\text{m}$.
For stress, $\text{N m}^{-2}$ is defined as the pascal, so stress has unit $\text{Pa}$. This rules out rows starting with newton.
For strain, $\text{m}$ divided by $\text{m}$ cancels, so strain is a pure ratio and has no unit. This rules out rows with metre for strain.
For Young modulus, use $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$. Since strain has no unit, $E$ has the same unit as stress, which is $\text{Pa}$.
Therefore the row is pascal, no unit, pascal. This is option D.

A.explanation: Stress is not force in $\text{N}$ and strain is not extension in $\text{m}$; stress is force per unit area and strain is a ratio of lengths.

B.explanation: Strain correctly has no unit, but stress is not $\text{N}$ and Young modulus is not $\text{N}$ because both involve division by area.

C.explanation: Stress correctly has unit pascal, but strain is not in $\text{metre}$ and Young modulus is not in $\text{newton}$.

D.explanation: Stress is in $\text{Pa}$, strain has no unit, and Young modulus $= \text{stress}/\text{strain}$ is in $\text{Pa}$.
